title: #theatre #westend #studioghibli #spiritedaway #hayaomiyazaki
transcript: as a huge Studio Ghibli fan I couldn't pass up the opportunity to see the stage adaptation of one of my favourite films of all time, Spirited Away this is a big spectacle entertainment show that uses puppetry and elaborate costuming just to bring to life all of the magical moments and characters from the film and that is absolutely the joy of the show I definitely enjoyed the experience but I'm very glad that I went in with the proper expectations knowing that this was kinda just gonna be the movie on stage it is very faithful to the film maybe to a fault like it doesn't really feel like it has much of an identity of its own and it does feel like we're kinda just moving through the plot beats of Spirited Away rather than like experiencing a story with its own sense of flow and I think part of the reason for that is that the film is obviously brilliant but it is kind of slow and meditative and a little bit neandering at times it obviously works because Miyazaki's vision was so crystal clear and he had full control over the execution but then when you kinda try to copy and paste that into the medium of theater it becomes a little bit untethered from what was holding all the pieces together one exception where I did feel like the show kind of had an identity of its own was in the addition of the dance and also the use of movement for the characters which definitely did feel like different in some places from the film especially with the character of No Face the way that he moved was very specific and cool the other thing for me is that it was just so incredibly special to be able to hear Joe Hisaishi’s iconic score played by a live orchestra I know sometimes symphonies will do it and stuff but I've just never been able to get to one of those performances so it was a first for me by the way in case anyone is wondering no I have not yet seen the stage adaptation of my Neighbor Totoro I would very much like to the timing has not worked out but I hope to get the opportunity soon overall I know that I criticized this but I definitely would recommend it as long as you kinda go in knowing what to expect you're there for the spectacle and the puppetry and all that stuff
